newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore industrial output up after five-month fall.
newsitem.headline: Singapore industrial output up after five-month fall.

text.p: Singapore's manufacturing output for April rose by 1.1 percent year-on-year after five consecutive months of decline, the Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Monday.
The EDB said the rise was due to higher output in the electronics, chemicals and transport equipment industries.

"The electronics industry recorded an increase in output for the first time in 1997. Output grew by 3.1 percent with more production of disk drives, computer peripherals and telecommunication equipment," the EDB said.
However, production levels of personal computers and semi-conductors were still below those of 1996, it said.
Cummulative output for electronics in the first four months of 1997 was seven percent lower that in the same period in 1996, the EDB said.
Electroncis account for about half of Singapore's industrial output and 60 percent of non-oil domestic exports.
The rise in April manufacturing output was expected as the government had earlier announced April non-oil domestic exports were up 5.9 percent, said Sim Shyh Yang, economist at Keppel Securities.
But Sim said the recovery was not broad based. "April's output growth may have been helped by strength in specific sectors such as semi-conductors."
Other areas of the economy which showed increases in April included chemical industries, where output rose by 4.7 percent.
The transport equipment industry grew by 6.3 percent in April, boosted by output in the aviation segment though output in the marine segment continued to decline.
